'''Dual control theory''' is a branch of [[control theory]] that deals with the control of systems whose characteristics are initially unknown.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Feldbâum |first=Ά. Á. |date=1963-06-01 |title=Dual control theory problems |journal=IFAC Proceedings Volumes |series=2nd International IFAC Congress on Automatic and Remote Control: Theory, Basle, Switzerland, 1963 |language=en |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=541–550 |doi=10.1016/S1474-6670(17)69687-3 |issn=1474-6670|doi-access= }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Wen-Hua |last2=Rhodes |first2=Callum |last3=Liu |first3=Cunjia |date=2021-11-01 |title=Dual Control for Exploitation and Exploration (DCEE) in autonomous search |url=https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/Dual_Control_for_Exploitation_and_Exploration_DCEE_in_autonomous_search/16577825/1/files/30684152.pdf |journal=Automatica |language=en |volume=133 |article-number=109851 |doi=10.1016/j.automatica.2021.109851 |s2cid=228372721 |issn=0005-1098}}</ref>  It is called ''dual'' because in controlling such a system the controller's objectives are twofold: 
* (1) '''Action''': To control the system as well as possible based on current system knowledge
* (2) '''Investigation''': To experiment with the system so as to learn about its behavior and control it better in the future.
These two objectives may be partly in conflict.
In the context of [[reinforcement learning]], this is known as the exploration-exploitation trade-off  (e.g. [[Multi-armed bandit#Empirical motivation]]).

Dual control theory was developed by [[Alexander Aronovich Feldbaum|Alexander Aronovich Fel'dbaum]] in 1960.  He showed that in principle the [[optimal control|optimal]] solution can be found by [[dynamic programming]], but this is often impractical; as a result a number of methods for designing sub-optimal dual controllers have been devised.

==Example==

To use an [[Car analogy|analogy]]: if you are driving a new car you want to get to your destination cheaply and smoothly, but you also want to see how well the car accelerates, brakes and steers so as to get a better feel for how to drive it, so you will do some test manoeuvers for this purpose.  Similarly a dual controller will inject a so-called probing (or exploration) signal into the system that may detract from short-term performance but will improve control in the future.
